targets.name: actionlint-workflows
targets.subsystem: GitHub Actions syntax, expressions, and embedded shell
targets.oracle: actionlint exits zero after enumerating every workflow; embedded Bash runs through installed ShellCheck.
targets.coverage_method: Every .github/workflows YAML file is listed in the retained log
targets.known_gaps: actionlint cannot prove runtime Actions semantics or artifact provenance; exact-head CI jobs do that.

targets.name: zizmor-workflows
targets.oracle: zizmor exits zero with no actionable offline audit findings over every enumerated workflow.
targets.coverage_method: Every .github/workflows YAML file is listed in the retained log
targets.known_gaps: Offline mode omits online audit checks; zizmor still reports default-suppressed findings whose policy is not yet independently audited.

targets.name: gitleaks-branch-commits
targets.subsystem: secret exposure in new repository commits
targets.oracle: Gitleaks scans every commit after the exact merge-base, emits a fully redacted JSON report, and returns zero with zero findings; missing reports and scanner errors fail.
targets.coverage_method: Printed merge-base and commit count; scanner report covers the exact branch range
targets.known_gaps: The PR gate scans new commits, not all historical objects or the current working tree. A current-tree exploratory scan reported 16 redacted candidates; a history scan timed out after 120 seconds with 27 candidates. Neither is claimed clean or broadly suppressed.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains the redacted report and scanner log.

targets.name: full-make-verify
targets.engine: GNU Make, GCC, Clang, Rust, host assertions
targets.oracle: The unmodified make verify recipe and every child test, fixture digest, and kernel invariant must return zero. A failed child is a failed target.
targets.execution: host Linux and produced kernel image
targets.coverage_method: Existing host assertions and kernel artifact checks; no guest execution claim
targets.known_gaps: The Makefile's verify target does not run all 115 QEMU scenarios; guest checks remain separate. It cleans build before testing.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Make verify deletes its own build tree; runner evidence lives in verification/runs and is retained.

targets.name: runner-failure-sentinel
targets.oracle: A temporary harness-only assertion must produce a failed_finding step with exit code 1 and retained stderr; the injected source is removed afterward.
targets.coverage_method: Direct failure classification; no OpenRFS kernel coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: This checks assertion propagation, not every signal/timeout/interruption path.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Retains logs; removes only its own temporary injected source.

targets.name: host-baseline
targets.subsystem: first-party lint and existing host smoke tests
targets.engine: GNU Make and GCC host tests
targets.oracle: Existing host assertions and trailing-whitespace gate return zero; every child failure is propagated by Make.
targets.coverage_method: Existing assertion receipts; no source coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: This fast baseline is only two host test binaries and lint; the repository's full make verify runs separately in extended CI.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains unique logs; Make owns build/tools.

targets.name: shellcheck-firstparty
targets.oracle: ShellCheck exits zero at warning severity for every tracked first-party shell script; script enumeration must be nonempty.
targets.coverage_method: Tracked script enumeration and static diagnostics, not runtime execution
targets.known_gaps: Vendored upstream scripts are excluded from the first-party gate and remain an explicit separate review scope.

targets.name: ruff-firstparty-python
targets.subsystem: first-party Python tooling, tests, and proof generation
targets.engine: Ruff 0.16.9 targeted correctness rules and Python annotation regression
targets.oracle: Ruff F821/F822/F823/B006 finds no correctness diagnostics in enumerated first-party Python; typing.get_type_hints resolves the UI font failure annotation.
targets.coverage_method: Every scanned Python file is printed; static diagnostics only
targets.known_gaps: Vendored Python is excluded; broader style and security heuristics are not represented by this gate.

targets.name: clippy-firstparty-rust
targets.subsystem: kernel Rust boundary, native ABI and app, ext4 transaction host tests
targets.oracle: Pinned Clippy returns zero with correctness lints denied for every first-party Cargo manifest; a changed manifest inventory fails closed.
targets.execution: host Linux and x86_64-unknown-none Rust target
targets.coverage_method: All four tracked first-party Cargo manifests are enumerated; static diagnostics only
targets.known_gaps: Style and pedantic groups are outside this gate; vendored Rust crates are dependencies, not first-party lint targets. Clippy does not prove guest behavior.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains logs; Cargo owns build/verification-clippy-target.

targets.name: package-transaction-sequence
targets.subsystem: package install, rollback, recovery, and user data isolation
targets.oracle: An independent single-package model checks version, generation, owned file contents, user data, and complete resource cleanup after each versioned operation; cut recovery selects only old/new allowed states.
targets.coverage_method: Hypothesis examples and per-operation counts; no Python line-coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: This exercises the Python transaction coordinator and in-memory fault model. It does not prove kernel package signature admission, raw disk ordering, or QEMU restart durability.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains unique logs and minimized failure bytes when present.

targets.name: package-state-parser
targets.subsystem: package trust and durable generation metadata
targets.oracle: Admitted database record views remain in bounds and encode into an admitted authority; admitted authority and journal fields obey fixed size and generation invariants; ASan/UBSan/LSan must remain silent.
targets.coverage_method: LLVM source coverage from instrumented production C replay; libFuzzer edge counters for campaigns
targets.known_gaps: The fuzzer does not prove Ed25519 verification, package installation I/O, or QEMU executable admission. A valid signed fixture and guest transaction campaign remain needed.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner creates a unique directory and never removes another run.

targets.name: acpi-madt-topology
targets.oracle: Successful topology has a bounded enabled local APIC and I/O APIC; every rejection zeroes topology; ASan/UBSan/LSan must remain silent.
targets.coverage_method: LLVM source coverage from instrumented production C replay; libFuzzer edge counters for campaigns
targets.known_gaps: The host adapter uses MAP_32BIT for the kernel's identity-mapped physical pointer convention. It tests MADT topology after root-table admission, not RSDP discovery or real APIC MMIO lifecycle.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner creates a unique directory and never removes another run.

targets.name: multiboot2-admission
targets.subsystem: boot information admission, memory map, framebuffer, and ACPI tags
targets.oracle: Known valid tags are admitted with bounded pointers and a readable memory-map region; malformed tags reject; reused context resets after a bad magic call; ASan/UBSan/LSan must remain silent.
targets.execution: host Linux x86_64 with MAP_32BIT early-physical adapter
targets.coverage_method: LLVM source coverage from instrumented production C replay; libFuzzer edge counters for campaigns
targets.known_gaps: The host mapping models reachable physical bytes with zero-filled memory beyond the saved input; it cannot prove firmware ownership, unavailable physical pages, the boot assembly handoff, or device initialization after parse.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner creates a unique directory and never removes another run.

targets.name: valgrind-package-replay
sanitizers: Memcheck and leak check, independent of ASan
targets.oracle: A plain Clang build of production package_state.c replays all eight committed valid and invalid seeds under Memcheck; every expected admission result matches and Memcheck reports no errors or leaks.
targets.coverage_method: Eight named seed replays and per-seed Memcheck logs; no new source coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: Only the host-built package metadata parser and eight saved inputs are checked; Memcheck does not instrument the guest kernel or cover fuzz-generated inputs here.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains the binary and all per-seed logs.

targets.name: c-static-focused
targets.subsystem: package metadata, ACPI topology, and Multiboot2 admission parsers
targets.oracle: Clang Static Analyzer exits zero with warnings treated as errors over four production translation units with the kernel's target flags.
targets.coverage_method: Explicit four translation units printed in log; no dynamic coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: This gate covers four files only. A broad exploratory analyzer run over all kernel C files found candidate warnings and one missing vendor include, retained separately for triage.

targets.name: clang-tidy-focused
targets.subsystem: package metadata, ACPI topology, and Multiboot2 admission parsers
targets.engine: clang-tidy 18 targeted bugprone and core analyzer checks
targets.oracle: Selected bug-prone and core checks exit zero with diagnostics treated as errors on actual C source and flags.
targets.coverage_method: Explicit four translation units printed in log; no dynamic coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: Limited to reviewed correctness checks and four production files; broad style and vendor code excluded.

targets.name: cppcheck-focused
targets.subsystem: package metadata, ACPI topology, and Multiboot2 admission parsers
targets.oracle: Cppcheck exits zero with warning, performance, and portability diagnostics as errors over four production files.
targets.coverage_method: Explicit four translation units printed in log; no dynamic coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: Only four reviewed files are gated; compiler-specific freestanding constructs may need separate Clang review.

targets.name: qemu-production-matrix
targets.subsystem: guest process, fault teardown, filesystem persistence, TCP listen, and native network wait slots
targets.engine: QEMU 8.2.2 TCG and existing Makefile scenario oracles
targets.oracle: Each actual guest run must satisfy its existing strict expected exit, begin/pass receipt, no panic, and subsystem diagnostics; serial SHA must match the retained copy. TCP and native network scenarios require resource teardown censuses; native network must report readiness on the later of two wait slots.
targets.coverage_method: Six scenario-result.json receipts and serial traces; no guest source coverage claim
targets.known_gaps: Only six of 115 existing scenarios run here. No general guest syscall sequence generator or durable power-cut injection is present. Non-network cases lack a uniform resource census.
targets.cleanup_behavior: Runner retains copied evidence; Make owns generated scenario artifacts. QEMU jobs are serialized by runner lock.

targets.name: qemu-normal-boot
targets.subsystem: kernel boot, self-tests, and deterministic serial contract
targets.oracle: Existing qemu-test-normal checks the expected debug-exit and required serial diagnostics; a boot banner alone is insufficient.
targets.coverage_method: Existing scenario receipt and serial log, not guest source coverage
targets.known_gaps: This scenario does not exercise filesystem persistence, networking, or native process teardown; the broader existing matrix remains separate.
targets.cleanup_behavior: The runner retains its logs; Make owns build/tests/normal. QEMU jobs are serialized by runner lock.
